pr.title: coverage: Restrict empty-span expansion to only cover `{` and `}`
pr.description:
Coverage instrumentation has some tricky code for converting a coverage-relevant `Span` into a set of start/end line/byte-column coordinates that will be embedded in the CGU's coverage metadata.

A big part of this complexity is special code for handling empty spans, which are expanded into non-empty spans (if possible) because LLVM's coverage reporter does not handle empty spans well.

This PR simplifies that code by restricting it to only apply in two specific situations: when the character after the empty span is `{`, or the character before the empty span is `}`.

(As an added benefit, this means that the expanded spans no longer extend awkwardly beyond the end of a physical line, which was common under the previous implementation.)

Along the way, this PR also removes some unhelpful code for dealing with function source code spread across multiple files. Functions currently can't have coverage spans in multiple files, and if that ever changes (e.g. to properly support expansion regions) then this code will need to be completely overhauled anyway.
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.originalLogic: In the historical `InstrumentCoverage` lowering from a coverage-relevant `Span` to `SourceRegion`, `make_source_region` first looked up the source file from `span.lo()`, rejected `!file.contains(hi)` as a multi-file span, then computed 1-based line numbers and byte columns. For an empty span (`span.is_empty()`) contained in the function body span, it then always tried to make the span non-empty by nudging one character boundary: prefer the end if `hi < body_span.hi()` using `src.ceil_char_boundary(hi_rpos + 1) - hi_rpos` added to `end_col`; otherwise, if `lo > body_span.lo()`, subtract `lo_rpos - src.floor_char_boundary(lo_rpos - 1)` from `start_col` with `saturating_sub(nudge_bytes).max(1)`. The comment said: "Prefer to expand the end position, if it won't go outside the body span." It also stored a per-mapping/function `file_name` and grouped mappings by that filename.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation being replaced was an unconditional/near-unconditional one-character expansion of any empty coverage span, regardless of which character was adjacent. Thus an empty span immediately after `}` and before a newline could be expanded past the physical line end instead of covering the `}`, and empty spans adjacent to spaces, newlines, or other non-brace characters were also expanded. The corrected transformation returns a non-empty span unchanged; for an empty span it expands only when the source byte after the span is `{` and `hi < body_span.hi()`, or when the source byte before the span is `}` and `body_span.lo() < lo`; otherwise it returns `None`. This is a policy/behavior simplification, not a confirmed bug report, so do not present it as a reproduced bug.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs compiled with coverage instrumentation where coverage-relevant `Span`s can be empty, especially spans associated with block/brace regions: single-line `if cond { ... }`, closing braces at end of line, blocks before newlines, closures, async functions, match arms, loops, doctests, and Unicode/multibyte source. Relevant input distinctions are the byte immediately after an empty span (`{` versus newline/space/other), the byte immediately before it (`}` versus other), and whether the empty span is at the function body span boundary. Functions are assumed to have all coverage spans in the same file as `body_span`.
analysis.summary: Coverage span lowering in `InstrumentCoverage` changed empty-span expansion from a general one-character nudge to a brace-specific rule. An empty span is now expanded only to the following `{` or preceding `}`, within the function body span; otherwise it is skipped. This avoids expanding empty spans over arbitrary characters and past physical line ends. File identity for the function's mappings is now taken from `FunctionCoverageInfo::body_span`, because a function's coverage spans are currently assumed to be in one file. Focused coverage tests should compare brace-adjacent empty spans with identical spans adjacent to newline/space/non-brace bytes, plus body-boundary and Unicode cases.
analysis.trigger: During coverage instrumentation, `make_source_region` receives an empty span. The historical code expands it by one character boundary in either direction; the corrected code invokes `ensure_non_empty_span` and expands only if the next source byte is `{` or the previous source byte is `}` (subject to body-span bounds).
preconditions: The span is empty (`span.is_empty()`), otherwise compression/expansion should not alter it.
Source text is available from `SourceMap::span_to_source`; if not, the expansion fails and the region is skipped.
Expansion toward the next byte requires `hi < hir_info.body_span.hi()`; expansion toward the previous byte requires `hir_info.body_span.lo() < lo`.
The next byte must be ASCII `{` for forward expansion, or the previous byte must be ASCII `}` for backward expansion.
All of a function's coverage mappings are currently expected to be in the same file as its `body_span`; per-mapping file names are no longer used for the file table.
pitfalls: Do not simply drop all empty spans: LLVM's coverage reporter handles empty spans poorly, so brace-adjacent empty spans should still become non-empty.
Do not expand every empty span merely to make it non-empty; arbitrary expansion misattributes coverage and under the old code commonly extended beyond a physical line.
Guard byte indexing at body-span edges: do not read `src.as_bytes()[end]` when `hi == body_span.hi()`, and do not read `src.as_bytes()[start - 1]` when `lo == body_span.lo()`.

Line/column coordinates are 1-based and columns are byte offsets, not character counts; the old character-boundary nudging could interact badly with multibyte Unicode. The new check only needs ASCII braces.
An empty span after `}` should expand backward to cover `}` rather than forward over the following newline/character.

Do not rely on per-region `file_name` for grouping; the patch removes it and derives the function's file from `body_span`. Reintroducing multi-file grouping without redesigning the metadata would be incorrect under the current assumption.
The existing `check_source_region` ordering/range validation still applies after expansion, and doctest line offsets are applied after line/column computation.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/coverage` and `tests/mir-opt/coverage` style checked outputs (`.cov-map`, `.coverage`, and `InstrumentCoverage` MIR dumps). Construct paired source variants that differ only in the byte adjacent to an empty coverage span: (A) an empty span followed by `{` versus an otherwise identical empty span followed by newline/space/other; (B) an empty span preceded by `}` versus an otherwise identical empty span preceded by another character. Include a single-line `if cond { body(); }` where the closing-brace region is empty after `}` and before a newline; the corrected output should place the region on the `}` (caret one column earlier), while the old behavior placed it beyond the line content. Add body-boundary cases where no forward/backward expansion is allowed, and a Unicode/multibyte case to ensure byte-column handling does not resurrect character-boundary nudging. Update MIR expectations to show `coverage body span: ...` and file-less `coverage Code(...) => start_line:start_col - end_line:end_col;` entries. No compiler was built for this analysis; these are source-patch-derived test strategies, not execution results.
